source.title: Some open problems in the theory of topological groups and semigroups

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a Hausdorff countably compact paratopological group G, where paratopological means that the group multiplication map G x G -> G is continuous, that is not a topological group because the full topological-group continuity requirements fail?
Must every Hausdorff countably compact paratopological group G, where the group multiplication G x G -> G is continuous, be totally bounded?

Let G be a Hausdorff semitopological group, meaning that G is a group with a topology such that multiplication is separately continuous and inversion is continuous. If the underlying topological space of G is Baire, must G be a topological group?

Does there exist a Hausdorff minimal paratopological group that is not a topological group, where minimal means that its topology is a minimal element among the relevant Hausdorff group or paratopological group topologies on the same group?

Given any paratopological group (G, tau), where tau is a Hausdorff topology making multiplication continuous, does there always exist a coarser or equal group topology tau' <= tau such that (G, tau') is a topological group?

For a Tychonoff space X, let I(X) be the free topological inverse semigroup over X: a topological inverse semigroup equipped with a topological embedding of X and satisfying the universal property for maps from X into topological inverse semigroups. Is I(X) itself Tychonoff for every Tychonoff space X?
For a zero-dimensional topological space X, is the free topological inverse semigroup I(X) over X also zero-dimensional?

Which classes P of topological spaces have the following recognition property for free topological inverse semigroups: whenever I(X) is homeomorphic to I(Y) and X belongs to P, it follows that Y also belongs to P?

Let S be a topological inverse semigroup, let E(S) be the subsemigroup of idempotents of S, and let H = {H(e) | e in E(S)} be the family of maximal subgroups of S. Given topological properties P_1 and P_2, if E(S) has property P_1 and each maximal subgroup H(e) has property P_2, what topological properties must the whole semigroup S have?

In the preceding topological inverse semigroup setting, suppose P_1 and P_2 are both metrizability and S is compact. If the idempotent subsemigroup E(S) is metrizable and every maximal subgroup H(e) is metrizable, must S be metrizable?

The local shard outputs/open-problems-0418-all.csv identified zbMATH 1366404 as 'Some open problems in the theory of topological groups and semigroups'. Exact-title search recovered a matching readable PDF at Matematychni Studii.

Mapped a three-page PDF. Page 223 contains the title, definitions of semitopological and paratopological groups, prior compactness results, and Problems 1-4. Page 225 contains references and affiliation only.
